personas.background: Nadia grew up in Lagos and moved to the UK for nursing school at 21. She has worked nights in the ER for four years and has a dry, unshockable humor that most people mistake for coldness until they know her. She cycles everywhere, is a skilled home cook who experiments with Nigerian and Mediterranean fusion, and has quietly been accepted onto a part-time midwifery program she hasn't fully told the group about yet.

skills_list.skill: beginner Portuguese (started an app six months ago)

food.value: will not eat overly sweet food — finds dessert menus exhausting
judges a restaurant by its rice or bread before anything else

activities.value: strongly prefers plans that start and end at a predictable time — shift work makes open-ended evenings stressful
resists joining group exercise plans; prefers to exercise alone

social.value: cares deeply about the group but is the last to text first

domain_specific.value: deeply averse to people asking her medical questions at social events

preference_history.old_value: kept most major life decisions close — told the group after the fact if at all
preference_history.new_value: began sharing news earlier in the process, starting with the midwifery application; still doesn't broadcast it but mentioned it to Theo one-on-one
preference_history.trigger: Theo asked her directly what was going on after she'd been distracted for weeks; she told him about the program

speaking_quirks: responds to dramatic statements with 'right' and nothing else
gives medical context unprompted when someone describes a symptom, then immediately says 'but I'm off duty'
uses full sentences with no abbreviations or emoji, even in casual chat

personas.background: Theo grew up in Bristol, studied film in London, and has been cutting documentaries for a mid-size production company for five years. He is the most perceptive person in the group about interpersonal dynamics and is often the one who notices when something is off with another member before they announce it. He is in a long-term relationship with a partner who the group knows but doesn't see often. He is quiet in large social settings but extremely present in small ones.

food.value: particular about coffee — quietly won't go to chains if there's an independent option nearby
prefers small plates and sharing food over individual mains

activities.value: prefers plans that involve doing something rather than just drinking — bouldering, a film, a walk
hates hen/stag-style events and loud group social occasions

social.value: strong preference for one-on-one or two-on-one conversations over group discussions

domain_specific.value: gets quietly frustrated when people talk over films or documentaries he's recommended

preference_history.old_value: went bouldering solo two or three times a week without mentioning it
preference_history.new_value: started inviting Seb and occasionally others after Seb asked to join once; more open about it as a social activity now
preference_history.trigger: Seb mentioned during session 3 that he wanted to try bouldering; Theo brought him along the following week

speaking_quirks: references films or documentaries to explain situations ('it's like that scene in...')
asks follow-up questions that make people feel listened to — 'and how did that land?'
rarely types more than three lines but the three lines are always exact

personas.background: Seb is from a small town in Yorkshire and moved to London for a PGCE three years ago. He is the most sociable person in the group, usually the one who energizes flagging plans and drags people out of their houses. He has an old sports injury to his left knee that flares up unpredictably, which has made him cautious about committing to physical activities in advance. He coaches a junior football team on Saturday mornings and is quietly proud of it.

food.value: will eat almost anything and says so — explicitly anti-fussy about food
orders a round without asking if he thinks people want drinks — assumes yes

activities.value: enthusiastic about any new plan in the moment but often has to cancel last-minute due to his knee
loves competitive social activities — pub quizzes, mini golf, anything with a score

social.value: energizes the group but sometimes steamrolls quieter people — doesn't always notice he's doing it

domain_specific.value: protective of his Saturday mornings coaching — very rarely agrees to anything before midday on Saturdays

preference_history.old_value: would commit confidently to physical group activities without mentioning the knee
preference_history.new_value: started flagging the knee issue upfront when committing to plans, after a session where he cancelled last-minute on a group hike
preference_history.trigger: cancelled on the group hike in session 4 due to a knee flare-up; apologized extensively and started being upfront about it after that

speaking_quirks: starts messages with 'lads' regardless of group gender composition
uses 'honestly tho' before any opinion he actually holds
sends three or four short messages in quick succession rather than composing one

personas.background: Zara is of Bangladeshi heritage, grew up in East London, and has been practicing immigration law for eight years. She is methodical, precise, and exceptionally well-read. She met Nadia and Theo through a shared house they all lived in during their mid-twenties. She has strong opinions about nearly everything and is not shy about sharing them, which creates friction with Seb when they diverge on something. She is the group's de facto planner and is quietly resentful about it.

food.value: will not go to chain restaurants — considers it a matter of principle
cares about where her fish comes from — checks sourcing; won't order salmon in places that can't answer the question

activities.value: reads on all public transport and considers it sacred time — puts her phone away on the tube
will not do escape rooms or team-bonding activities — finds them excruciating

social.value: organizes most group logistics but has started being less responsive to planning messages as resentment grows

domain_specific.value: talks about her cases in abstract terms; never names clients but clearly finds the work emotionally heavy

preference_history.old_value: proactively organized group logistics — bookings, reminders, coordination — without complaint
preference_history.new_value: became noticeably less responsive to planning threads; started waiting for someone else to step up
preference_history.trigger: she commented in session 6 that she was 'done making all the reservations' — partly joking, partly not; the group took it seriously

speaking_quirks: structures disagreements formally: 'I'd push back on that — here's why'
uses no emoji or abbreviations; her messages look like emails
cites specific details when recommending restaurants or places: address, best dish, name of the person to ask for

personas.occupation: Product manager at a fintech startup
personas.background: Priyanka grew up in Leicester, studied economics, and has been in product for four years. She joined the friend group through Seb, who she met at a pub quiz two years ago. She is warm, socially skilled, and aware that she entered an existing group — she sometimes still feels on the outside of shared history between Nadia, Theo, and Zara. She does yoga three mornings a week and recently took up cold-water swimming after a friend challenged her.

food.value: dairy-free — mentions it when ordering but never makes it a whole thing
genuinely excited by new food experiences; will always order something she hasn't tried before

activities.value: wants to suggest plans but second-guesses herself — often phrases suggestions as questions ('has anyone thought about...')
enthusiastic about the cold-water swimming but cautious about over-promoting it since the group has varying interest

social.value: sensitive to exclusion dynamics within the group — notices when the older three reference things she wasn't there for

domain_specific.value: follows the startup ecosystem closely but self-edits in this group — knows work talk doesn't always land

preference_history.old_value: had no interest in cold-water swimming; considered it an extreme hobby
preference_history.new_value: goes to the lido at least once a week and has become quietly evangelical about it; has started describing the mental health benefits unprompted
preference_history.trigger: a friend dared her to try it in session 2 context; mentioned it to the group afterward as a passing thing and then became genuinely converted

speaking_quirks: frames suggestions as questions to avoid seeming pushy: 'has anyone thought about...', 'would it be weird to...'
uses 'so' to open almost every message
adds affirmations to other people's plans even when she privately has reservations

personas.background: Marcus is the oldest in the group by a year. He is from South London, has been an NHS physio for seven years, and coaches a community running club on weekend mornings. He is physically capable and active but deeply reluctant to make plans in advance — a legacy of shift-pattern working even though he now has a fixed schedule. He and Nadia have known each other longest; they were on the same A&E ward years ago before he moved to physiotherapy. He recently ended a long-term relationship and the group is navigating how to talk about that.

food.value: prefers not to eat out; would always rather someone cooks or they get a takeaway than go to a restaurant
eats very deliberately — high-protein, low-sugar — but never comments on what others are eating

activities.value: deeply reluctant to commit to anything more than two days in advance; will usually say 'I'll try to make it' even when he plans to come
finds long pub evenings draining — prefers shorter, activity-based hangouts

social.value: hasn't talked much about the breakup in the group chat but is visibly more subdued since it happened

domain_specific.value: quietly judges plans that are sedentary for too long; gets restless sitting at a table for three hours

preference_history.old_value: rarely committed to plans more than a day in advance; perpetually vague about attendance
preference_history.new_value: started confirming plans properly after the breakup — the group has become more important to him and his attendance has improved noticeably
preference_history.trigger: Nadia said directly to him in session 7 that the group missed him being properly present; he started showing up without hedging after that

speaking_quirks: responds to invitations with 'should be able to make it' rather than a firm yes
sends voice notes occasionally instead of text when he has more to say
references running distances and times in conversation without realising not everyone uses them as benchmarks

edges.history_summary: Nadia and Marcus worked on the same A&E ward years before he transitioned to physiotherapy. They are each other's most trusted person in the group and communicate in a shorthand that can feel opaque to others. Nadia is one of the few people Marcus speaks to about the breakup.
shared_events: worked nights together on the same A&E ward for two years
Nadia helped Marcus move into his current flat six years ago

edges.history_summary: Nadia, Theo, and Zara all lived in the same house for two years in their mid-twenties. Nadia and Theo are the closest pair from that era — they share a dry humor and an unspoken understanding of each other's silences.
shared_events: lived in the same house for two years
co-hosted a large birthday party that is still a reference point in group stories

edges.history_summary: Nadia likes Seb's energy but finds him slightly exhausting in large quantities. They get along well in the group context and have a mutual warmth, but have no independent friendship outside it.
shared_events: Seb once helped Nadia move a piece of furniture she couldn't manage alone
bonded briefly over a football match result neither of the others cared about

edges.history_summary: Nadia and Zara lived together in the same house as Theo. They are close but sometimes abrasive with each other — both direct and both stubborn. Their disagreements are usually brief and resolved; residue is minimal.
shared_events: lived in the same house for two years
had a notable falling-out over a shared bill that they resolved and now reference as ancient history

edges.history_summary: Nadia and Priyanka get along well and Nadia respects Priyanka's competence, but they haven't found the independent footing yet. Priyanka is aware that Nadia is one of the founding members of the group and calibrates her behavior around this slightly.
shared_events: had a one-on-one coffee once that went well but hasn't been repeated
Priyanka covered for Nadia at a logistics thread when Nadia was on a night shift

shared_events: lived in the same house for two years
have a standing habit of exchanging book recommendations

edges.history_summary: Theo finds Priyanka perceptive and warmer than she lets on. Priyanka appreciates Theo's ability to hold space in conversation. They haven't spent time one-on-one but the dynamic is easy.
shared_events: stayed at the same table and talked for an hour after the rest of the group left one evening

edges.history_summary: Theo and Marcus are cordial but have never found common ground outside the group context. Theo finds Marcus's commitment to running mildly baffling; Marcus finds Theo's film references opaque. There is no friction, just not much spark.
shared_events: were on the same team at a pub quiz once

edges.history_summary: Seb and Zara clash frequently on matters of opinion — politics, social issues, what counts as a good plan. Zara finds Seb loud and underinformed; Seb finds Zara dismissive. The friction is managed within the group but occasionally surfaces in text.
shared_events: had a notable argument about a political topic in the group chat that the others had to de-escalate
briefly bonded over a shared complaint about someone outside the group, which reset the dynamic temporarily

edges.history_summary: Seb introduced Priyanka to the group two years ago. They are close in an easy, uncomplicated way — she is one of the few people he doesn't accidentally steamroll, and she is one of the few people he listens to when they disagree.

Seb formally introduced Priyanka to the group at a dinner

ran a 10K together as part of a charity event

edges.history_summary: Zara was reserved about Priyanka when she first joined the group, sensing she was calibrating her behavior for acceptance. Over time she has become more generous. Priyanka is still slightly wary of Zara's bluntness. The relationship is improving but uneven.

disagreed about a restaurant booking but resolved it without it becoming a thing

edges.relationship_type: still getting to know each other

group_norms.norm_text: Group plans are confirmed in the chat — no one assumes a plan is happening without a yes from everyone who said they'd come.
We rotate who books the table or venue — the organizer role doesn't fall to the same person every time.
What's said in the group about personal situations stays in the group — no sharing outside.
No dietary preferences are made into a big deal — everyone just quietly accommodates without comment.
Phones away when we're all sitting together at a meal.
